digest_pin.message: digest mismatch: bytes hash to 7fca157f055e but <config>/graph_pin.toml pins 4790bbb1111b - corruption or tampering, not staleness (the file is kept on disk and a fresh graph is built; allow_graph_digest_mismatch opts into reusing it)
bypasses_tried: internal space in digest (MATCHED: 12-hex prefix comparison)
digest_pin.bypass_found: no SILENT bypass. Two fail-open degradations, both reported in the stage line but with NO note: unreadable/malformed/missing/empty/mis-keyed pin degrades to unpinned => tampered graph reused as 'unverified'. Weakness: comparison uses only the first 12 hex chars of the pinned value, so a pin with a wrong tail still reports match.
digest_pin.override_behaviour: reuse, with digest_state=mismatch in counts and a loud note 'graph: DIGEST MISMATCH ... reused only because allow_graph_digest_mismatch opted in'; not reachable from the CLI (run --help has no such flag)
digest_pin.control_boundary: An attacker who can write only state/kg/.../graph.json is caught: the bytes no longer match the pin, so by default they are not reused, the reason is loud and the file is kept. An attacker who can also write (or delete, deface, or re-key) config/graph_pin.toml is not caught -- a consistently replaced graph+pin is reused as digest_state=match, and destroying the pin downgrades the control to unpinned+reused.
